title: cldr export writes through a temporary file
objective: `cldr export` writes its CSV through a temporary file and a rename, as `render` and `briefing` do, so an interrupted export never leaves half a CSV in place of a whole one; `--force` stays the only way to replace an existing CSV. Every write error names its file, as `intent/llm/RULES.md` requires: today `create_dir_all` and `std::fs::write` in `export_command` report a bare OS error.
context:
Landed as 22074cc; cldr-vc reviewed it (the code is right, gates rerun green in a fresh clone). Its review's follow-ups landed as 7cd73c1, on cldr-vc's verdict:

- F1: AC-01 (an export replaces its CSV whole, no temporary file left), AC-02 (every write error names its file or folder) and AC-03 (`--force` is the only way to replace a CSV), covered by AT-01 to AT-05, the five `cli.rs` tests.
- F3: `a_failed_write_names_the_file` asserts the full CSV path.
- F4: `write_csv` takes export's `--force` refusal and its folder out of `export_command`, and the folder's error has its test.
- F5: a failed write or rename removes `<file>.cldr-tmp`, in render, briefing and export alike, and the error says so when it cannot.
- cldr-vc's V1 to V3: the temporary file is synced before the rename; the tests' folder listings fail on an entry they cannot read; the CHANGELOG's 0.2.3 says what changed.

criteria.text: An export replaces its CSV whole, through a temporary file and a rename, so an interrupted export never leaves half a CSV in place of a whole one, and no temporary file is left behind, whether the write succeeds or fails.
Every write error an export reports names its file or its folder.
--force is the only way to replace an existing CSV: without it, an export refuses, names the CSV and leaves it as it was.

tests.note: cli::tests::a_failed_rename_leaves_no_temporary_file; red against the old write_atomically, which left calendar.csv.cldr-tmp
